scope: Repair the merged P6 correctness defects without expanding architecture ownership: remove P6-private persistence/canonical truth, bind P6 persistence/replay evidence to the existing M6 authoritative recovery stack and P4/M4/P5 canonical owners, make PENDING/OperationId handling fail closed, replace simulated restart evidence with a real process-boundary gate, and retract false soak/visual completion claims until literal evidence exists.
required_outputs: P6 has zero filesystem writer and zero private save format
P6 canonical mutations route to accepted M4/P4/P5 owners rather than P6OutpostState
Replay durability is delegated to the existing M6 authoritative recovery stack
PENDING retry cannot execute a handler twice
OperationId history is never forgotten in a way that permits re-execution
Restart proof crosses an actual process boundary with persisted bytes only
Literal 30-minute two-client soak and MCP visual evidence are required before P6 may be re-accepted
stop_conditions: Repair would require a new persistence owner or P6-private save format
Repair would require a second Item Graph, Construction truth, equipment store or replay oracle
Repair would require changing NX/gateway/network authority foundations
Literal soak or MCP evidence is unavailable: remain FIX_REQUIRED/VERIFYING; do not fabricate PASS
risk_reasons: Repairs persistence and replay semantics after a merged checkpoint

design_brief.problem_statement: Merged P6 introduced a P6-private persistence owner, a duplicate mutable outpost truth and an in-memory replay ledger whose PENDING and retirement semantics can re-execute operations. Restart and soak evidence overclaimed the literal product predicates.
design_brief.current_behavior: P6 tests can pass by persisting a private P6OutpostState and carrying ledger snapshots through the same test process; old OperationIds can be retired and PENDING retries can be admitted again.
design_brief.desired_behavior: P6 is a composition/read-model boundary only. Canonical Item Graph, equipment, Construction and persistence/replay remain with the accepted M4/P5/P4/M6 owners. Recovery uses authoritative checkpoint + replay_state across a real process boundary. Incomplete literal soak/MCP gates remain visibly incomplete.
design_brief.selected_design: Fail closed all P6-private mutation/persistence surfaces, convert P6 helpers to adapters/read models over existing canonical owners, keep transient in-flight reservations non-durable, and require the canonical M6 replay owner to prove completion. Use the existing authoritative recovery repository/coordinator for process restart evidence.
alternatives_considered: Persist the P6 ledger beside the P6 outpost file
Increase the compressed soak loop count
Keep P6OutpostState as canonical and document it as an owner
expected_risks: Legacy P6 focused tests depend on private mutable state and must be replaced rather than weakened
A repair that marks transient PENDING as durable would recreate a second replay oracle
Control evidence must preserve the historical false PASS while explicitly superseding it
non_goals: No gateway or transport foundation change
validation_plan: Static zero-write fence over all P6 runtime modules
Focused PENDING retry and OperationId retirement regressions
Canonical-owner composition regression against existing P4/M4/P5/M6 public surfaces
Two-process restart/recovery test using only existing authoritative checkpoint bytes
Fresh Reviewer and Verifier on exact repair head
design_brief.why_selected: It repairs the defects at their canonical ownership boundaries instead of strengthening the duplicate P6 stack that violated the original Work Order.

notes: This R3 repair supersedes the correctness claims of the merged P6 R2 candidate but does not rewrite its append-only history. Until all R3 predicates pass, P6 must be treated as merged-but-FIX_REQUIRED rather than a valid accepted predecessor for SM1/P7.
